National Assembly
XX Session
Proceedings Details
25 Chaitra 2082
Wednesday
Meeting
Number -
National Assembly's meeting today commenced at 13:20 hrs under the chairmanship of the Right Honourable Chairperson Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable members, names of Honourable members have been presented to speak during the Zero Hour. (13:20 hrs) I have allocated 1 minute of time to each Honourable member to speak during the Zero Hour. First, Honourable Member Gita Devkota.
Honourable Mr. Gita Devkota (Nepali Congress):- Right Honourable Chairperson, I wish to draw the serious attention of the government through you, Chairperson, to the fact that the lives of common people are becoming extremely difficult due to the price hikes caused by the conflict in the Middle East. (13:21 hrs) Our country is primarily agricultural, yet farmers producing vegetables, food grains, fruits, milk, fish, meat, etc., need to be made professional in the long term. For this, I wish to draw the government's attention, through the Honourable Chairperson, to adopt a policy of encouraging farmers by bringing short-term and long-term concrete programs through the upcoming budget, strengthening production, storage, and transportation management. Thank you. Jai Nepal.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Dharmendra Paswan.
(13:22 hrs)
Honourable Mr. Dharmendra Paswan (Nepali Congress):- Right Honourable Chairperson, the incident in Ward No. 3 of Surunga Municipality, Saptari District, occurred on the 30th of Falgun. The victim, Manju Kumari Sadar, aged 14, was kept in that house for domestic work. She was then... by having sexual relations and inflicting punishment. The deceased is Maheshwor Prasad Yadav. The son is Mukund Yadav. The relative is Dharma Devi Yadav. The helper is Binda Yadav, who is also a ward member. Chairperson, through this house, I urge the government to take action for justice as soon as possible. Thank you.
(13:22 hrs)
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Mr. Minasingh Rakhala.
(13:23 hrs)
Honourable Mr. Minasingh Rakhala (Communist Party of Nepal, UML):- Right Honourable Chairperson, Karnali, which holds potential from its water and land, today I stand in this respected house carrying the pain of Karnali and seek answers. (13:23 hrs) Despite abundant resources, why is Karnali lagging behind and poor? Karnali has immense water resources, vast land, fertile soil, but sadly, the government's attention does not reach it. All these... are being wasted. Rivers are being polluted, but Karnali remains in darkness. Resources are abundant, but the people are not benefiting. There is land, but no access to production and markets. Chairperson, this is not a natural scarcity. It is the neglect and failure of the state. Remember Karnali not in speeches but in the budget. Therefore, I demand through this respected house: Invest immediately in Karnali's water resources. Keep the utilization of water resources centered on the local people. Bring special programs for agriculture and infrastructure. Karnali does not need charity; Karnali needs rights and opportunities. If arrangements are not made now, silence... (Time expired).
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Rekha Kumari Jha.
(13:25 hrs)
Honourable Mr. Rekha Kumari Jha (Communist Party of Nepal, UML):- Right Honourable Chairperson, similar to every year, there is a shortage of chemical fertilizers, and this year too, due to the war between America, Israel, and Iran, a situation of further shortage is arising. The government should be serious and procure the necessary chemical fertilizers for the upcoming season in a timely manner. (13:25 hrs) Right Honourable Chairperson, the problem of farmers being displaced due to the destruction caused by monkeys and other wild animals in various parts of the country, especially in the hilly regions, which occurs every year, should be resolved immediately, and I also demand that relief and compensation be provided to the affected farmers. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Mr. Lalit Jung Shahi.
(13:26 hrs)
Honourable Mr. Lalit Jung Shahi (Nepali Congress):- Right Honourable Chairperson, Transparency International's 2024 report, which evaluates the state of corruption in various countries worldwide, ranks Nepal 109th out of 182 countries, and with 34 points out of 6, it has been proven to be a corrupt country. (13:26 hrs) I wish to draw the serious attention of the Government of Nepal, through the Right Honourable Chairperson, that the current government with a strong majority should seriously contemplate declaring Nepal a corruption-free country with good governance. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Samjhana Devkota.
(13:27 hrs)
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Somnath Poudel.
(13:27 hrs)
Honourable Mr. Somnath Poudel (Communist Party of Nepal, UML):- Right Honourable Chairperson, according to government data, the population of the oppressed Dalit community in Nepal is 3,898,990. Due to the declared policies of the past feudal state system, this community has been suffering economically, socially, and in terms of human rights, except for arts and skills. (13:27 hrs) In this situation, I heartily welcome the current government's public declaration to apologize again to the oppressed Dalit community from the state. I wish to remind the government by quoting the words of the people's leader Madan Bhandari: "Words do not soak rice." I urge the government to immediately announce special programs for economic and social transformation by effectively implementing the current constitution and laws. I want to inquire from the government about the progress of the programs, including the entrepreneurship development programs, put forward by the government led by KP Sharma Oli, with adequate budget. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- The order for Honourable members to speak during the Zero Hour concludes here. (13:28 hrs) Names of Honourable members have been presented based on party representation to speak during the Special Time. Now I will provide time for Honourable members to speak. First, Honourable Member Sunil Bahadur Thapa, time 9 minutes. After this, Honourable Member Jayanti Devi Rai.
Honourable Mr. Sunil Bahadur Thapa (Nepali Congress):- Right Honourable Speaker, Honourable Members, (13:29 hrs) Today, I wish to present important issues before this house. The constitutional parliamentary process, which was disrupted by the general elections held on the 29th of Falgun, has resumed after overcoming a difficult political situation. It is well known that the current national politics is based on the foundation of the Janji rebellion of August 23rd and 24th. Its management and analysis are being done by various security agencies. While the questions and arguments are valid in their own right, democracy has triumphed through the provincial assembly elections that resulted from the Janji rebellion, and the constitution has survived. I feel this is a major historical turning point in the politics of South Asia, including Nepal. Secondly, I want to draw attention to a serious international issue like the conflict in the Middle East. In this era, any international conflict affects the entire world. Its impact is even greater in a landlocked country like Nepal. Given that our energy and supply depend on India, I urge the Government of Nepal to closely monitor this situation and coordinate with the Government of India to ensure a continuous supply of fuel. Furthermore, the increase in fuel prices will have a serious impact on the overall economy. In this regard, I welcome the decision of the Honourable Finance Minister to reduce taxes and other indirect duties on fuel imports, but I also urge the government to permanently reduce or review such indirect taxes in the long term. It is essential for our economy to have affordable fuel prices. I wish to express my views on national politics. For the past six decades, Nepal has been plagued by political instability. The time has come for all political party leaders to rise above personal interests and prioritize the nation. We must all believe in the supremacy of the constitution. We need to build capable institutions and safeguard the rule of law. The success of democracy depends not only on lawmaking but also on its impartial implementation, and it greatly affects the government's conduct. In this context, what the country needs most today is compromise and reconciliation. At present, Nepal cannot afford any kind of political instability. Seeing the division seen in the political sphere today spread to the public level, I consider it the responsibility of the Government of Nepal to end this social and political division as soon as possible. Nepal's history is a history of sacrifice, struggle, and change. From the Rana regime to multiparty democracy, and then to a federal republic, the Nepali people have made many sacrifices for their rights. The value of those sacrifices is today's democracy. But the question arises: have the people truly experienced the reality of democracy as they desired? Through the Right Honourable Speaker, I wish to draw the attention of the Government of Nepal that the Nepali Congress has played a leading role in every movement in Nepal. Furthermore, the Nepali Congress's understanding and movements have led to peaceful resolutions. For this, I also urge the Government of Nepal to learn from the path shown by Nelson Mandela. Nelson Mandela succeeded in bringing democracy to South Africa, overcoming potential ethnic violence. He united the country. He avoided the temptation of thinking that justice was delivered by suppressing the political opposition and chose the path of reconciliation, coexistence, and a shared future. I sincerely request the Government of Nepal to follow this same path. His foresight, generosity, and tolerance played a significant role in establishing peace and stability in South Africa. Additionally, the new government should act in accordance with the aspirations of the people, including the spirit of the youth rebellion of August 23rd and 24th, the fundamental tenets of the constitution, freedom of press and expression, human rights, independent judiciary, checks and balances of power, the spirit of coexistence and cooperation, good governance, and efficient service delivery. We must resolve all past mistakes and injustices through legal means without any political prejudice. However, the current government has a golden opportunity to develop a new political culture based on tolerance, respect, and cooperation in parliamentary practice. The responsibility for establishing such a culture now rests on the shoulders of the government. Regarding money laundering, we have closely observed every incident. In this context, I also wish to draw attention to line 16 of the Rastriya Swatantra Party's manifesto. Nepal now needs to develop a culture of impartial cooperation. This will further strengthen our democracy. Climate change, which has affected the world, has not spared Nepal. Nepal is the most vulnerable country in terms of climate change. Therefore, the temperature of the Himalayas is increasing. The main impacts include melting glaciers, erratic monsoons, and floods, which lead to increased landslides, soil erosion, and droughts. These impacts directly threaten agriculture, hydropower, and livelihoods. Mass migration is under stress. The destruction of hilly local livelihoods and agricultural land promotes large-scale migration. Many are heading towards densely populated urban centers in South Asia. Therefore, I request the Government of Nepal to give full attention to this issue and bring special programs for it immediately.

I would like to draw attention to the problems faced by farmers in Dhankuta district. The problem of monkey infestation, lack of irrigation, and increasing water scarcity. This is the reason why people are forced to go abroad for employment. Due to the increasing menace of monkeys, farmers are suffering huge financial and agricultural losses. I would also like to draw the attention of the government, the Ministry of Forests, Agriculture, and other relevant ministries to solve this serious problem. Also, the country has high expectations from the new government. But the expectation is for reconciliation and finding solutions. It is about chasing only one party or person and surrounding them, representing the justice of every single person. Therefore, I request the Government of Nepal to consider tolerance and look at everything justly in the days to come. Finally, as the National Assembly is mature and responsible, we are all present here to play our expected role accordingly. We will play a constructive and cooperative role, and we expect a similar role and behavior from our friends from other parties. The National Assembly is a forum for problem-solving. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Jayanti Devi Rai, time 9 minutes. After this, Honorable Member Samjhana Devkota. (13:38 hrs) Honorable Ms. Jayanti Devi Rai (Nepal Communist Party):- Honorable Chairperson, I first (13:39 hrs) heartily welcome the newly elected members of the National Assembly, congratulate them heartily, and wish them success in their work. I also extend my heartfelt congratulations and best wishes to the current government, including the Honorable Prime Minister and the entire government team. Chairperson, regarding the circular issued by the Council of Ministers on Chaitra 18 and 19, this circular has become highly controversial even before its implementation. And the decision in the said circular that only government-owned media can publish government advertisements and private media cannot is extremely wrong and undemocratic. I want to ask why the government is repeatedly making controversial decisions. Today, this decision will empower all private media and gradually snatch away the right to freedom of the press. I demand that this undemocratic and autocratic decision be corrected immediately. Today, let's see, to establish this system and this right, media persons were at the forefront of the movement, and thousands shed blood, and heads were broken. Similarly, day by day, the government sometimes bans student organizations and sometimes makes decisions to restrict press organizations. This should not be forced. Today, the right of these students to have a large organization and the right to speak is being snatched away. Today, the government needs to think about this. We don't want to speak about the government today. Because it is such a popular government, a government that has gained so much public trust. But we couldn't remain silent today. Today, we have given the government our best wishes for success, and we expect from the government that all the established movements that have established the nation must be institutionalized. Not to snatch away their rights, but to institutionalize the established rights and ensure the remaining rights. To fight for the remaining rights, for the rights of the people. We had faith that this government would do this. Therefore, I want to request and urge the government not to make such decisions and to correct them. Chairperson, for some time now, criminal incidents of cyberbullying against adolescent girls have been increasing alarmingly. In the last 4 months, these incidents have occurred in the range of 2,009, almost 3,000. Today, thousands of adolescent girls with dreams are mentally devastated by this incident. They are physically weak and socially insecure. If we do not look into the problems of such youth today, what kind of society are we building? What kind of youth power are we preparing? Therefore, those criminals who take obscene photos of adolescent girls in the name of AI, post them, use obscene language, and threaten them with rape, are roaming freely, fearlessly, and openly. Today, victim women have to face life and death thousands of times, with no guarantee of survival, not even security. I want to urge the Home Minister, Home Minister, didn't these youths support you in thousands in the movement? I want to say again, from this respected assembly, do not break the trust of those youths, and create an environment where these youths with dreams can freely fulfill their dreams. Stop this cybercrime today and use this cyber bureau effectively and appropriately. We know, we have discussed many times in the National Assembly, we have had very serious discussions. The Social Media Bill in the Legislation Committee, the government has withdrawn that Social Media Bill. The government must immediately bring back this withdrawn bill. Strict action must be taken against criminals related to this online violence, digital violence. We should not accept the established notion that anything can be done, anything can be said. We should not establish that notion. Therefore, I want to request, and the people wanted change, and parties with a long history once supported the public in this way. Therefore, there is a Nepali proverb, "Do not rejoice in happiness, do not despair in sorrow." Therefore, I want to urge today. Today, the future of all youth is heading towards darkness, and all judicial systems are becoming defunct. The public is getting this impression. Therefore, I want to give them suggestions in a very positive way, not negatively, and we also aspire to have a stable government. We were demanding a stable government. Now, this majority government will be a stable government, and we believed that society would truly prosper without any disruption in a stable society. Today, the general public has the same faith, but many decisions have been made in such a short period. Thank you for that, but your decisions are undemocratic, they must be corrected, and I am happy today. No party had the provision of 33 percent women in the cabinet, but today's government has fulfilled the 33 percent women quota for women. But today, let women not be victims. I would like to end my speech here. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Samjhana Devkota, time 5 minutes. After this, Honorable Member (13:48 hrs) Mohammad Khalid. Honorable Mr. Samjhana Devkota (Nepal Communist Party, UML):- Honorable Chairperson, the current government, which has pledged to work on issues like good governance, impartiality, accountability, transparency, and anti-corruption, and has received invaluable and extraordinary public mandate from the Nepali people, has shocked us with its very first step. We have been forced to raise the same issue repeatedly. At a time when we should be uniting to put the country on the path of development and prosperity, and accelerate it, we are focused on the same issue. That is the illegal and unconstitutional arrest of the Chairman of the CPN-UML party and former Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli, which has saddened us all. I demand the immediate release of the government. I am shocked by the unfortunate incident of Bhadra 23 and 24. No one is above the law and the constitution. I demand appropriate legal action against those involved in that incident. Honorable Chairperson, the number of Nepalis going to the Gulf countries in search of employment is extremely high. 52 workers who came to work at Hussein Bin Ali At Fast Company in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, after facing various difficulties with the dream of supporting their families, have been in a miserable condition for a week without wages and work, as seen in videos. I request the government to investigate the truth and take appropriate steps to protect their employment and lives. Honorable Chairperson, I express my serious concern about the insecurity of Nepalis living in the Middle East due to the ongoing war between Iran and Israel, America. I want to draw the attention of the Government of Nepal to ensure the safety of Nepalis in that region. Due to the same war, the extreme price increase of petroleum and gas has led to inflation of daily necessities, and the hearths of Nepalis are about to go out. I want to draw the government's attention to this. There are many gas companies in the market. Even now, we have to face many difficulties to get gas. One company does not agree to exchange cylinders with another company, and even if they do, we have to pay 500 rupees to exchange the gas. This may seem like a minor issue, but it is a very difficult issue in daily life for low-income and middle-class families. I want to draw the attention of the Government of Nepal through the Chairperson to create a situation where these companies can exchange gas without charging money. Honorable Chairperson, I want to alert this assembly to the trauma suffered by our daughters and women due to cyberbullying incidents. A serious question has been raised about social values and norms, and about us Nepalis. This is an issue for all Nepalis. Nepal, which has become a party to international conventions, covenants, and the Beijing Declaration against Gender Violence, wants to end all such social evils. In the meantime, social media and cyberbullying have become an easy tool for financial online fraud and character assassination. Thousands of women and children have fallen victim to this. Cyberattacks against women have become an easy, sharp, and effective weapon for character assassination. Women are being killed every moment. Such attacks on women and children not only harm individuals but also damage the honor and respect of the entire family and family relationships. I want to draw the attention of the Government of Nepal to control this cyberbullying. Through our honorable women ministers, I request the Government of Nepal to enact strict laws and regulate this. I want to draw the attention of the Government of Nepal to find ways to easily solve the technical and financial difficulties faced by the Cyber Bureau to make it active. Finally, I would like to extend my heartfelt congratulations to the newly elected Vice-President and the chairpersons of the committees of this National Assembly and wish them a successful tenure. Thank you. Presiding: Honorable Vice-President Mr. Lila Kumari Bhandari.

(13:52) Honorable Chairperson:- Honorable Member Mohammad Khalid, time 6 minutes. After this, Honorable Member (13:53) Tul Prasad Bishwakarma.
Honorable Mr. Mohammad Khalid (People's Socialist Party, Nepal):- Honorable Chairperson, I would like to congratulate all the elected honorable members of the National Assembly and wish them a successful tenure. I would also like to congratulate Honorable Lila Bhandari on being elected as the Vice-Chairperson of the National Assembly and the chairpersons of the four committees, and wish them a successful tenure. Let us once again, with firm resolve, move forward to further elevate the dignity of the National Assembly and work according to the interests and aspirations of the country and the people.
Honorable Chairperson, recently, Rastriya Swatantra Party achieved historic and unprecedented success in the general elections held for the House of Representatives. They secured 48 percent of the votes, for which I congratulate that party, its chairman, and all its leaders. I also congratulate the newly formed government and wish them a successful tenure. I also want to state that there is no one elected from that party in the Parliament here. However, I want to say one thing about the National Assembly, through you, Honorable Chairperson, that there has never been a "for" or "against" in the National Assembly. In my four years of experience, even when my own party's government was in power, the honorable members here supported good work and opposed decisions that needed opposition. This is the history of the National Assembly. Therefore, through you, Honorable Chairperson, I want to tell the current government that you will find both supporters and opponents here. Today's governments have received 48 percent of the votes. The people have high hopes from it and are ready to evaluate it. Political instability is a major problem in Nepal. Political problems, because before this, they did not receive votes close to two-thirds. Will the current government make good choices instead of ours? Will corruption be reduced comprehensively or one-sidedly? Will the debt burden increase or decrease? What will be the state of economic growth? Will imports be controlled or not? Will inflation be controlled or not? Will the operation of industries and factories remain limited to today's speeches or be streamlined? What will be the state of balanced foreign policy? The issue of press freedom will be raised. The diagnosis of problems related to the end of all forms of discrimination, political, administrative, economic, and social justice, and constitutional amendment is also a major concern for many now. I also support and welcome the government's decision to include all political parties in the task force formed to pass the constitutional amendment. Let the MPs and parties from various backgrounds and parties become each other's allies. Because we are not enemies. We are working for this Nepal. The country can only move forward through dialogue, consensus, and cooperation. As I conclude, I will say one thing, "Even if there are a million enemies, do not end the relationship; whether hearts meet or not, keep shaking hands."
Honorable Chairperson:- Honorable Member Tul Prasad Bishwakarma, time 5 minutes. After this, Honorable Member (13:59) Narayan Datta Bhatta.
Honorable Mr. Tul Prasad Bishwakarma (National Janamorcha):- Honorable Chairperson, clouds of an undeclared world war are hovering over the skies of the Middle East, and the Iranian people are enduring immense suffering there. Today, this war has created ripples globally and has caused immense pain to justice-loving and peace-loving people worldwide. America has threatened to push Iran back into the Stone Age again 23 days ago. Barbaric attacks are also happening there. Iran has rejected the ceasefire proposal of 45 days put forth by America and has put forward its own proposal for a complete cessation of hostilities, which is a just demand for peace. Looking at America, by examining its history, we know that it has a history of oppressing weak nations worldwide, showing bullying tactics, and spreading terror globally. Even now, Trump has announced the occupation of Greenland, attempting to occupy many countries. The ambassador of Argentina has been abducted. There is a threat of attack on Cuba; such a situation has arisen. The entire world is in conflict with Trump's terrorist policy. Not only Russia, China, and North Korea, but even NATO countries and India have increasing conflicts with America. Within America itself, 8 to 9 million people have taken to the streets against Trump. Despite this situation, his threat to push Iran back into the Stone Age actually confirms that Trump himself is becoming weaker within his own country. We congratulate the Iranian people who are resisting America's imperialist terrorism. Their resistance is not just for Iran but is also a part of the global struggle against imperialism for the people of the world. Therefore, Nepal, along with all peace-loving people worldwide, has an international responsibility to oppose this oppression, bullying, and imperialist terrorism by American imperialism. Therefore, we hope that the Iranian people resisting this imperialist terrorism will be victorious, and the peace-loving people of the world, along with the people of Iran, will be victorious. Therefore, today this war has had a global impact. It has also affected our country. Inflation is rising, there is a shortage of oil, and its impact is being felt in various forms and dimensions within the country. Therefore, I demand that the current government pay timely attention to all these matters, formulate policies and programs accordingly to provide the necessary facilities to our people and make their lives easier, and pursue them with promptness. Thank you.
Honorable Chairperson:- Honorable Member Narayan Datta Bhatta, time 9 minutes. After this, Honorable Member (14:04) Bhuvan Bahadur Sunar.
Honorable Mr. Narayan Datta Bhatta (Nepali Congress):- Honorable Chairperson, respected honorable members, first of all, I extend my best wishes for a successful tenure to all the newly elected honorable members of the House of Representatives and the National Assembly. I also extend my best wishes for a successful tenure to the Vice-Chairperson of the National Assembly and the chairpersons of the standing committees.
Honorable Chairperson, today there is a government with nearly two-thirds majority; may the government be successful. May the Nepali people witness good deeds for five years. Although we lost in the popular vote, we have not lost in ideology. The government should be mindful. But the issue is, what about the safety of our Nepali brothers and sisters who have gone to the Gulf countries to earn a living? Will they be safe? Will they be able to return to their country? Secondly, with the current rise in inflation, the hearths of the poor and common people have reached a dire state; what about that? I see the government has a two-thirds majority. I was discussing this in my village, wondering what would happen now. I believed that whether we did well or poorly, because democracy was established, Rastriya Swatantra Party is now close to a two-thirds majority. It is a well-known fact that establishing democracy is difficult, and they lack experience. But if this government is moving towards a path where anything can be done in politics, abandoning the promises made to the people with fanfare and extravagance, it seems so. This country has various units: administrative units, courts, various offices. If the work of all these offices has ended, then let's just write "District Office" and "Province Office." There are rules, laws, procedures. If the Home Ministry is to do all the work, then why are these district administrations kept? Therefore, my request is, it's fine, let's prepare a report named Gauri. Today, let's give a name like Gauri to something that has a name, and tomorrow we'll make another Gauri. But will the current Prime Minister and Home Minister take responsibility for the murder of the youth in Nawalparasi? Will sections 081 and 082 of the penal code apply to them? This is my question to the government. Therefore, I want to request, don't just think about me; justice will be served, whether late or soon. This country belongs to all of us. Therefore, I humbly request you to remember your responsibilities.
What about the investigation into Sudhan Gurung's matter concerning the Home Minister in Pokhara? Rabi, poor Rabi, and Chhabi, what about them? What is your stance? This is my question from this house. If Rabi does not want to be called guilty, but has been accused, the same accusation is against Chhabi. Why is Chhabi not considered "poor" and why is there a reason for his resignation? Therefore, as you raise issues, be mindful. It is right for the people to distrust us today, but this does not mean the party has lost. The party's ideology is why the honorable minister is here today. We have supported the good work you have done from this very house. But this is not new; you are not everything today. Those sitting here, those outside, and those who fought against you are only not honorable members. There might be 2000, 200, 300, 400 of them, but they are also the people. If you have 45 percent, remember that 55 percent is outside. Therefore, the issue is, if we do not proceed based on rules, procedures, and systems, we will not progress anywhere. I want to say, it's fine. What is the problem of the citizens of this country today? Has there been any discussion? Trade with India and China has reached our land; I was confident about this government's silence. This government will do two things; I started a debate among the general public with firm belief. One is foreign policy; the foreign policy of this country is somewhat disturbed, and the government's sustainability depends on it. The other is economic policy. I want to ask the honorable minister here. This country is already in trouble. If our situation remains like this, and this country goes on the blacklist, what will happen then? I address the honorable personalities, including the honorable minister; tomorrow, everyone's fate will be the same. Where you are, I will also be there, so be mindful. Today, the need of this country is, if we cannot bring the disturbed foreign policy back on track, this country will face dire consequences. The other is, what crimes are KP Sharma Oli, Ramesh Lekhak, Narayan Datta Bhatta, and other honorable members sitting here involved in? Put them in jail according to the law and procedures. One day it will be your turn too; you might also go to jail. It's not a big deal; a crime is a crime. But justice is never green or yellow. Justice is justice. Justice must be delivered in a way that it is felt. I have a great responsibility today, a historic responsibility, and faith. Do you realize that the parliament building we reduced to ashes yesterday is needed today? If we transform necessity into passion with such a sense of duty, decisions made in passion...

He makes it brown, so please be mindful of this matter. I request this entire government, all the honorable members in the government, that this government should move forward with all the happiness of the people and all the problems that have arisen today. I conclude my remarks by assuring everyone's support and cooperation in that. Thank you. Jai Nepal.

Honorable Chairperson: - Honorable Member Bhuwan Bahadur Sunar. Time 8 minutes. After that, Honorable (2:93 PM) Member Meena Singh Rakhal.

Honorable Mr. Bhuwan Bahadur Sunar (Nepal Communist Party):- Honorable Chairperson, with the permission of the Chairperson, I wish to present my issues. First of all, I would like to extend my best wishes for a successful tenure to the newly elected Vice President and all the newly elected honorable members. My issue today is also related to agricultural land. The severe problem of the rights and interests of tenants on agricultural land has resurfaced. Does it mean that it was inactive yesterday and is becoming active now? There is hope. Article 51 (u) of the Constitution of Nepal mentions policy related to agriculture and land reform. In point 1 of that... ending the dual ownership and implementing scientific land reform keeping in mind the interests of the farmers. Point 2: Land ownership of those who are absent and those who live in Kathmandu or America. Those who do not stay on their land for decades... by consolidating land and increasing production and productivity. Point 3 mentions adopting a land use policy to increase agricultural production by fully supporting the rights and interests of farmers. It is mentioned that land management and agricultural commercialization, industrialization, and modernization will be done. But even now, landlords like migrants are harassing farmers again. They are starting to displace poor farmers who have been cultivating for generations. Landlords are taking out red capital to create difficulties, depositing collateral in banks, and initiating actions like auctioning land... They have started such activities. It is necessary for the Ministry of Land Management and Cooperatives, Poverty Alleviation to prioritize this and work on it. Information has been received that land that has been in possession since the time of grandparents is being taken away by showing fake deeds and using the administration, preventing cultivation, showing threats, and the sons of the village chiefs are harassing them. Thousands of bighas of land are lying fallow. They are also trying to make other lands fallow. The slogan 'Whose is the cultivation, whose is the land' should have been implemented, but it has not been possible, which is why this problem has arisen... Therefore, this powerful government should work by making the issues of farmers its first agenda.

The land reform program of 2021 BS was very important for Nepal, an agrarian country. However, due to the feudal landlords not implementing it fully, the tillers have been deprived of getting deeds in their names. Feudalistic thinking or remnants still remain. This government needs to take steps strictly to ensure justice in the interest of the farmers. There is still the issue of 'guti' and 'bitta', and it is ironic that rights are being lost due to not receiving full rights. For example, these problems exist in many places like Swargdwari in Pyuthan, Shera Darbar in Nuwakot, and Gorkha Darbar, etc. I draw the government's attention to work with honesty. Last year, the affected people and farmers protested and demonstrated at Maitighar Mandala, which is well known to all of us. This problem has not been resolved, and such incidents may happen again.

Therefore, I will move on to another issue. Nepal has many large arable lands, but they are dry lands without water. It is necessary to irrigate them to increase agricultural production and become self-reliant. Rivers flow near these lands and plains, and irrigation can be easily done. We have raised this issue in the house repeatedly, but the government is not listening. Similarly, the Budhi Gandaki 1200 MW multipurpose reservoir, which can produce electricity throughout the year, should be started soon. It has always been said that it will start, but it has not started. Similarly, the Gorkha rubber industry and Hetauda textile factory are said to be reopened, but it remains to be seen what kind of programs this government will bring. We hope that these closed industries will be reopened. The repair work of the historic Tundikhel airport in Palungtar needs to be completed soon, which is currently stalled. If that airport is operational, it will be convenient for the entire country including Manang, Lamjung, Gorkha, Tanahu, and that airport can also be developed as a training center in coordination with tourism. I conclude my remarks by demanding from the government to complete this important airstrip. Thank you.

Honorable Chairperson: - Honorable Member Meena Singh Rakhal. Time 5 minutes. After that, Honorable (2:22 PM) Member Khamm Bahadur Khanti.

Honorable Mr. Meena Singh Rakhal (Nepal Communist Party, UML):- Honorable Chairperson, women constitute 51 percent of Nepal's population, while 33 percent representation of women is ensured. Despite having 33 percent representation of women, violence against women has increased significantly in our country. Today, there are various forms of violence against women. There is domestic violence, social violence, political violence, economic violence, and various types of violence, including cyber violence. Honorable Speaker, I wish to raise a very serious and sensitive issue in this esteemed house today: the issue of violence against women and cyber violence. Today's era is the era of technology. We are dreaming of Digital Nepal. But the sad thing is that technology is increasingly becoming a medium for new forms of violence against women. There are many examples, but we can take the example of the Parajuli sisters. We protested against violence on the streets and made laws, but now women are unsafe in mobiles and social media. Character assassination, obscene comments, misuse of photos and videos, threats – these are all forms of cyber violence. This is destroying not only the self-respect of women but also their mental health. This is not just a personal problem; it is a social and national problem. Chairperson, many women today cannot raise their voices, cry out, or speak because their faith in getting justice is weak. Faith in getting justice is weak, the law on cybercrime is slow. Those who are guilty are not seen to be severely punished, and if women are not safe, society is not safe either. If women are not respected, the value of democracy will also be weakened.

Therefore, I want to demand from the government through this esteemed house that the victims must get justice. Strict and effective laws against cyber violence should be implemented, and looking at the data of cybercrime today, 90 percent of cases are pending but not implemented. The security and privacy of victimized women must be guaranteed. Cybercrime investigation should be made fast, effective, and technology-friendly. Digital ethics should be taught through public awareness programs. Women are the foundation of society, they are strength. All forms of violence against women should be ended. Violence against women has not made people safer. When thinking about the types of violence, the situation is arising where women have to leave their homes and society. Women are not safe. Due to this digital cyber violence, women are facing difficulties from looking at Facebook, Twitter, and other things. Honorable Speaker, those involved in cyber violence should be severely punished immediately. The Cyber Bureau should be empowered with technology, manpower, and authority. The state should guarantee security and respect for the victims. Finally, if this cannot be done, otherwise we will be forced to agitate in the streets and in the house. Thank you.

Honorable Chairperson: - Honorable Member Khamm Bahadur Khanti. Time 9 minutes. After that, Honorable (2:26 PM) Member Suresh Kumar Alemagar.

Honorable Mr. Khamm Bahadur Khanti (Nepali Congress):- Honorable Chairperson, Honorable Members, the four individuals who have been unanimously elected as chairpersons of the thematic committees: Development, Economic Affairs and Good Governance Committee, Law, Rights and Justice Committee, National Interest and Coordination Committee, and Public Policy and Good Governance Committee - Krishan Prasad Poudel, Krishan Bahadur Rokaya, Pooja Chaudhary, and Jayanti Rai. I wish them congratulations and best wishes. The unity shown in the National Assembly, which the press has called 'bond-bond', but what I understand is that it has shown maturity, and even though there is representation from various parties, it is a good start of cooperation, coordination, and a system by the respected leaders of the parties. Therefore, I believe that the respected leaders of various parties and the chairpersons of the thematic committees elected to these committees have made a commitment to work together, united, and in one place, which is the beginning of a good culture.

Now, due to the short time given to me, I would like to state a few things point-wise. After the elections of February 21, the Rastriya Swatantra Party has secured an overwhelming majority and is close to a two-thirds majority. Honorable Minister is also present before me. He is also a student of law. Therefore, I would like to address him and request him. The state and the government are our guardians. Guardians should not discriminate against anyone and should not deprive anyone of equal opportunities. As students of the constitution and law, no one should violate laws and regulations. When talking about freedom, from the UN Charter to various conventions, we are proponents of freedom. In the past, the style or language used, such as 'chased away' or 'driven away' the old political parties this time, may be in its place. Did the old parties fail to adjust to the time, circumstances, and events? The public or voters are not anyone's personal property. They want change, and embracing change is the most important aspect, in my opinion. Therefore, we should adopt the good policies taken by the previous governments and abandon the bad ones. What has become clear in recent days is that some mechanisms are actively involved in deliberately and intentionally inciting, creating disturbances, and splitting the major political parties. I would like to request the Honorable Minister that in a parliamentary system, the most important thing is that the opposition must be strong. The opposition itself is a 'waiting government', in my opinion. Therefore, if it is said that there will be no opposition after this election, is this government not heading in the wrong direction? Such an impression is being created. Therefore, I would like to request you all that the Gauri Commission report has come out like a hot cake. You must have also seen the Gauri Commission report, 907, its 6, and it is seen that it has gone beyond the TOR of the Gauri Commission report. I must tell you truthfully, standing on this roster, that the events of the 24th are not addressed in this report. Only the events of the 23rd are addressed, and along with that, I want to request in this full house that it has gone beyond its TOR...

It has gone outside. It has made recommendations. You all should see what recommendations it has made, as is in the report of the Gauri Commission. It has given how the private sector should be run. It is about the banking sector. It has given how the judiciary should be run. It has given how cooperatives should be run. It has determined how journalists and lawyers should be compensated or how they should be managed. The Truth and Reconciliation Commission has also been included within it. I don't think such an action should have been taken. I feel that it is everyone's responsibility to abide by the law within the limits and scope set for them. Therefore, the Gauri Commission's report is largely biased and vindictive. It is malicious, and it itself has recommended that the government of Nepal investigate, inquire into, and prosecute offenses under Section 181 (1) and Section 182 of the Muluki Criminal Code, 2074. What does this mean? The reports we have understood, the information we have known. With about 32 years of experience in this profession. As a law student, I have investigated myself, prosecuted myself. This tendency of specifying sections also shows that the Gauri Commission's report is wrong, malicious, vindictive, and based on political ideology. Currently, in the context of former Prime Minister KP Oli, Ramesh Lekhak, and Chandrakuber Khapung at that time, the government itself has interfered and asked for further evidence to be gathered and investigated. Can such partial recommendations be made? Should it not be submitted as is? Does the Gauri Commission have the authority to determine this? No. Therefore, I want the entire government to correct this, and through you, Mr. Chairman, I wish for this matter to reach the ears of the Government of Nepal. Similarly, the current international war between Iran, Israel, and America, the direct war happening in the Middle East countries. The international intervention and bombing that is happening. Should the Government of Nepal say something about this or not? Those things are also worth considering. Our victims are currently living in such a complex situation. Whether to rescue them or not is equally important, so I request the Government of Nepal through the honorable chairman regarding that matter as well. Similarly, many people are suffering from inflation. I also want to request the government to bring a special program for that. I see the issue of foreign policy here as very important, and in the context of foreign policy, our constitution also states that in the context of foreign policy, Nepal should make an independent foreign policy based on the principles of the UN Charter, respect for Nepal's sovereign power, territorial integrity, independence, national interest, and active participation in international law and world peace. We need to see if this is happening. When we talk about our neighboring countries, when we talk about our Lipulek, can the government remain silent? I feel that our positions must be clear. Similarly, regarding the private sector, journalists are facing discriminatory policies, and the government is considering the matter of not giving them advertisements. Currently, in the name of money laundering, individuals are being targeted with prejudice. The Money Laundering Act was amended on 2080/12/30, and in contravention of that amended act, individuals have been harassed. False cases have been filed even when there were no other issues. The action that has taken place is not right, and I feel the government should correct it. Similarly, regarding loans, I want to request that the decision made by the government is wrong. Thank you. Jai Nepal. Honorable Chairman: - Honorable Member Suresh Kumar Ale Magar. Time 8 minutes. After that (2:36 PM) Honorable Member Roshni Mechhe. 94 Honorable Mr. Suresh Kumar Ale Magar (Nepal Communist Party): - Honorable Chairman Sir, (2:37 PM) First, I want to offer some congratulations and best wishes. First of all, congratulations to the various honorable members who have been elected to the vacant post of Vice-Chairman of the National Assembly and the vacant posts of Chairpersons of various four committees. I want to extend my heartfelt congratulations to the elected honorable Vice-Chairman and honorable Chairpersons of the committees. Congratulations to you whether you are a woman or a man who has become the chairperson. I also extend my heartfelt congratulations and best wishes for your successful and fruitful tenure. Similarly, the cabinet was formed about 10-12 days ago. I want to extend my heartfelt congratulations and best wishes to the honorable Prime Minister and all the members of the Council of Ministers. I also wish them a successful and fruitful tenure. Although it was formed according to the calendar on the 13th, that number is considered unlucky according to the calendar. 13 is an unlucky number. However, even though it was formed with this unlucky number, I wish this number to be lucky for the government. Honorable Chairman Sir, Honorable Chairman Sir, a few days ago, this government decided to dissolve student unions in campuses. This decision is completely wrong and undemocratic. Because, Honorable Chairman Sir, student unions were born out of autocratic, dictatorial, and Panchayat systems. They are organizations that have emerged by fighting against the dictatorship of that system through rigorous struggle. These organizations did not come into being under any pressure. They were also the organizations that carried forward the politics of the banned political parties during the periods of autocracy and the royal Panchayat system. It is wrong to ban such organizations. I strongly oppose that decision and demand its dissolution. Perhaps this government does not need students, but we do. Because we need students, farmers, laborers, and people from various professions. Perhaps this government does not need them, that's a different matter. But we need them. If student unions themselves do wrong things, we will take action. We will take action against their leaders and their activists. We can even dissolve the organizations themselves, not the government. Therefore, the government must reconsider this matter. Perhaps the government only needs votes. During the elections, we heard, "Join your party. You don't need to come to our party, just cast your vote." We heard such things, but we are not like that. We need votes, and we need organizations. We need activists from various communities. Therefore, this needs to be considered. Similarly, Honorable Chairman Sir, elections are held in a democratic system. Elections can be impartial or biased. They can be without fraud or with fraud. Capturing votes, casting fake votes, moving ballot boxes around, offering food and drinks, alcohol, etc., are all part of it. But in this 21st century, with so much technological development, will there be high-tech fraud? Will there be digital rigging? I don't know. So, if any winner, any caste, or anyone using it can tell me. These are just my questions, my curiosities. Not any specific conclusion or finding. High-tech fraud, digital rigging. 96 Honorable Chairman Sir, the government formed on this unlucky number has definitely done some work. For example, no Prime Minister has ever been from the Madhesi community. In the history of Nepal, 40 Prime Ministers have been appointed so far. No Prime Minister has been from the Madhesi community. It was not from... Therefore, in this sense, historic decisions have been made, and work has been done. Similarly, a Dalit woman has become a cabinet minister. 33 percent women are included in the current cabinet. Many such good things have happened. These are definitely positive actions. We appreciate them. But will these good deeds, these populist actions, lead to other actions later? We are watching vigilantly. Honorable Chairman Sir, similarly, apologizing to the Dalits is also historic and something no one has done before. Although it is said to be within 15 days, about 12-13 days have passed. I am not aware of the government having apologized. However, the fact that the state has spoken with the communities it has oppressed is definitely a historic and commendable matter. We appreciate it. This government, as one honorable member said earlier, there is no ruling party in this National Assembly, but you don't need to be intimidated or scared by saying "it's not ours." Because this entire National Assembly will support or oppose based on the actions taken by the government, based on positivity and negativity. Do good work, we will clap. If you do bad work, we will oppose, criticize, and scold you. This entire National Assembly is such a body. Perhaps people from your side will also come here later, that will be a matter for then, but for now, we are neither your blind devotees nor your blind supporters. Let the government view the National Assembly in this way. I want to state this. If you do good work, this National Assembly will say "Salute" like Rajesh Hamal's dialogue, and if you do bad work, this National Assembly will be "iron." This government, the government that has come now, in coming like this, it feels like it has forgotten the principle of... the principle of punishment and the principle of relativity. Nothing is entirely good, nor entirely bad. ...Society happens. Therefore, the narrative that has been constructed is: everything new is good, all youth are good, everything old is bad, all the elderly are bad. It's not like that. We see youth in all the crimes that have happened today. Are all youth bad? No. We need to look at it in this way. Looking at it that way, youth are both good and bad, the elderly are both good and bad. We need to look at it this way, but it is not being looked at that way. If this government commits wrong, anti-people, anti-national acts, we can move towards a national liberation war. Since we have marched with a shroud tied to our heads in the people's war, we can live this borrowed life. Therefore, all patriotic citizens will oppose any anti-people, anti-national acts. With this, I conclude my remarks. Thank you. Greetings. Honorable Chairman:- Honorable Member Roshni Mechhe. Time 5 minutes. After that, Honorable Member (2:45 PM) Bishnu Kumari Sapkota. Honorable Mr. Roshni Mechhe (Nepal Communist Party, UML): - Honorable Chairman Sir, first of all (2:45 PM) I want to extend my heartfelt best wishes for success in their work to the newly elected honorable Vice-Chairman and the chairpersons of the four committees. Today I want to raise those issues that are deeply affecting the foundation of our democracy and the daily lives of ordinary citizens. Honorable Chairman Sir, the Government of Nepal, in the name of its administrative reform...

Control over the activities of student organizations and their dissolution, which has been prepared, is an attack on the heart of democracy. We must not forget that whether it was the autocratic Panchayat rule or the absolute monarchy. Whenever the nation's nationality and people's livelihood were in danger, student organizations stood as shields. Our constitution clearly guarantees fundamental rights and duties in Article 3. Student organizations are not just political nurseries; they are also protectors of democracy and potential for educational reform. I would like to present a vivid example here. It is the recent suicide case of Prakriti Lamsal. When the state mechanisms were silent, it was the political student organizations of Nepal that raised their voices on this issue and demanded justice. Their activism even drew the attention of student organizations in India, and this issue could have taken an international dimension. If these organizations did not exist, who would speak for the voice of the oppressed students? To try to dissolve such an organization, which has played such a glorious and just role in history, all at once is an extreme insult to the contribution they have made. I want to ask the government: Is the government trying to form a Youth Council like in a certain country? Instead of completely dissolving student organizations, I want them to be reformed in a timely manner. Let's make it a forum for more effective, logical debate. Therefore, I want to draw attention to the fact that the government should immediately withdraw this decision to dissolve student organizations in an undemocratic manner.

Honorable Chairperson, I want to draw the attention of this esteemed house to a dire and heartbreaking situation in the livestock sector, which is considered the backbone of our rural economy. The outbreak of highly contagious and deadly Bird Flu virus, which started in Morang district on the 4th of Chaitra, has now been confirmed in commercial poultry farms in Jhapa. In the name of controlling the infection, the government has destroyed more than 1 lakh 13 thousand chickens and ducks, and more than 2 lakh 11 thousand eggs. This is connected to the dreams and future concerns of thousands of farmers. Farmers who mortgaged their homes and land and took loans at high interest from cooperatives and banks are today watching their livelihoods destroyed before their eyes... and are distressed. This virus is not limited to birds; it also poses a serious risk to human health. Therefore, this is not just an agricultural issue; it is also a public health issue. Therefore, Honorable Chairperson, I want to strongly demand from the government that a high-level technical team be immediately mobilized to take scientific and effective steps to control this epidemic. It should be ensured that the affected farmers are provided with compensation as soon as possible, not just assurances. Thank you.

Presiding again: Honorable Chairperson Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal.
(At 2:49 PM)
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Bishnu Kumari Sapkota. Time: 9 minutes.
(At 2:50 PM)
9t
Honorable Ms. Bishnu Kumari Sapkota (Nepali Congress):- Honorable Chairperson, I want to extend my heartfelt congratulations and best wishes for a successful tenure to the Honorable Members of the National Assembly elected on the 11th of Magh, the Honorable Members of the House of Representatives elected on the 21st of Falgun, the Honorable Prime Minister of the Government of Nepal, Honorable Ministers, the Speaker of the House of Representatives, the Vice-Chairperson of the National Assembly, and the Chairpersons of the thematic committees of the National Assembly. I also want to pay heartfelt tribute to the great warriors and martyrs who sacrificed their lives from 2007 BS to 2082 BS in various periods for democracy, for establishing good governance, and for maintaining order and good governance.

Honorable Chairperson, the demands of the Janji movement by our brothers and sisters on the 23rd of Bhadra, 2082 BS, were extremely just. The explosion occurred due to the failure to end the corruption rampant in the country, administrative delays, and the lack of guarantee of good governance, despite extreme chaos. Although we have repeatedly raised these issues from the streets to the parliament, they were not heard. As a result, innocent Janji brothers and sisters had to lose their lives today. The country has suffered damage that will take decades to recover from. The government has initiated investigation and necessary action according to the report of the Karki Commission, which was prepared over a long period. The Nepali Congress is a party that believes in the rule of law, and our cooperation will be in this work. However, this investigation and action should proceed impartially based on facts. Because the innocent should not be framed, and the guilty should not go free. "The morning shows the day" – the morning determines the day, because time will determine how the government presents itself.

Similarly, the destruction that took place on the 24th of Bhadra in the name of Janji was not a movement; it was vandalism across the country. It destroyed our historical heritage, inscriptions, and documents, turning them into ashes. This is a disgrace in history and a black mark. It is unfortunate and a grave mistake to omit this from the Karki Commission's report and to hide the perpetrators. To forgive such perpetrators is to do injustice to future generations. Therefore, I want to draw the attention of the government through the Honorable Chairperson to seriously address this issue. We expect that the newly formed government after the Janji movement will proceed in accordance with the spirit of Janji and the wishes of the citizens. The Nepali Congress assures its full support and cooperation in all actions taken by the government in accordance with constitutional laws and regulations. We also inform you that if the government deviates from the track, we will not give any leeway and will firmly play the role of a strong opposition, keeping a close watch.

Honorable Chairperson, the initiatives the new government led by Prime Minister Balendra Shah has sought to start, such as meeting with MPs from all seven provinces and discussing and seeking suggestions on provincial development and budget, are commendable. To further strengthen and refine this, we should hold meetings and discussions with local and provincial representatives, gather in-depth discussions, experiences, and suggestions regarding development plans and budgets, and with foresight, create plans and budgets that are felt by all, including the long-neglected women, backward castes and ethnic groups, farmers, agriculture, religious and ethnic tolerance, and communities living in geographically diverse areas, ensuring their coexistence, mutual respect, and message of goodwill. We want to express our support for its strong implementation and systematic management.

99
Similarly, the distribution of responsibilities in the new cabinet with 33 percent women representation and allocation of ministries based on capacity, such as issuing smart licenses and important appointments like Rastriya Banijya Bank, courts, National Planning Commission, are positive steps taken based on merit rather than power-sharing. I wish them continuity and success.

Honorable Chairperson, the government also faces many challenges. It is necessary to move forward with cooperation, agreement, and understanding with civil society, human rights organizations, constitutional experts, intellectuals, political leaders, and all national and international stakeholders, not in haste, but with patience. The biggest challenges are border and geopolitical issues, the Lipulekh pass dispute, balancing trade with India and China, and protecting national dignity. I suggest that sensitive foreign policy and diplomatic issues be addressed.

On the other hand, the biggest expectation of the citizens in making the current government strong with a two-thirds majority is for the management of empty villages, arable land, forests, and wildlife, for bringing back the labor force and youth power that has gone abroad for employment, for creating employment, and for secure investment. The general Nepali citizens have placed great hope and trust in this government. The government should be sensitive to this and begin its work; it will not take long for the country to be built.

Honorable Chairperson, the increasing cyberbullying of teenage girls in recent times is extremely concerning. To control this, the government should enact stringent legal provisions, identify the perpetrators, bring them to justice immediately, and expedite legal action. 
Along with this, to prevent derogatory comments, trolling, and online abuse targeting adolescents, a nationwide awareness campaign should be launched, and efforts should be made to make the Nepal Police Cyber Bureau effective in this regard, through the Honorable Chairperson, I want to draw the government's attention.

Honorable Chairperson, with the onset of the monsoon, we need to be aware and make others aware in time about incidents like fires, wildfires, floods, landslides, and road blockages that occur every year in our country. Through the Honorable Chairperson, I want to draw the government's attention to this.

Honorable Chairperson, for transparent information about the condition of Nepali citizens affected by the conflict in the Middle East, the government should take diplomatic initiatives and establish an integrated online portal, through which all citizens can easily understand the actual situation. Therefore, through the Honorable Chairperson, I want to draw the government's attention to the prompt initiation of its construction and implementation. Thank you. Jai Nepal.

Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Members, the turn of Honorable Members to speak during special time is now concluded.
(At 2:59 PM)

sections.name: Opening
sections.summary_en: The National Assembly meeting commenced at 13:20 hrs under the chairmanship of Honourable Chairperson Narayan Prasad Dahal. The chairperson announced the commencement of the Zero Hour and allocated one minute to each speaker.

speakers.name: Narayan Prasad Dahal
speakers.topic: Opening of Zero Hour and time allocation

sections.name: Zero Hour
sections.summary_en: Honourable members raised concerns during the Zero Hour. Gita Devkota spoke about rising prices due to Middle East conflict and urged support for farmers. Dharmendra Paswan highlighted a case of child abuse and demanded justice. Minasingh Rakhala lamented the neglect of Karnali's potential and demanded investment. Rekha Kumari Jha raised the issue of chemical fertilizer shortage and monkey menace affecting farmers. Lalit Jung Shahi pointed out Nepal's low ranking in corruption and urged the government to focus on good governance. Somnath Poudel discussed the plight of the Dalit community and called for effective implementation of laws and programs.

sections.name: Special Time
sections.summary_en: Honourable members spoke during the Special Time. Sunil Bahadur Thapa discussed the political situation post-election, the Middle East conflict's impact on fuel prices, and the need for national unity and reconciliation, drawing parallels with Nelson Mandela's approach. He also highlighted the threat of climate change to Nepal.

speakers.name: Sunil Bahadur Thapa
speakers.topic: Political situation, Middle East conflict, climate change, national unity

sections.name: Opening
sections.summary_en: Honorable Member Jayanti Devi Rai raised concerns about the problems faced by farmers in Dhankuta district, including monkey infestation, lack of irrigation, and water scarcity, leading to economic losses and migration. She urged the government to address these issues and also called for tolerance and justice in governance. Honorable Member Samjhana Devkota welcomed the newly elected members and congratulated the government. She criticized a recent government decision restricting advertisements to state-owned media as undemocratic and demanded its correction.

speakers.name: Jayanti Devi Rai
speakers.topic: Farmers' issues in Dhankuta, government policies, and national unity

speakers.name: Samjhana Devkota
speakers.topic: Welcome to new members, government's media policy, and democratic principles

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: Honorable Member Samjhana Devkota criticized the government's decision to restrict advertisements to state-owned media, calling it undemocratic and a threat to press freedom. She also highlighted the increasing cyberbullying against adolescent girls and urged the government to take strict action against perpetrators and to reintroduce the withdrawn Social Media Bill. Honorable Member Mohammad Khalid expressed concern over the illegal and unconstitutional arrest of former Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli and demanded his release. He also raised issues of Nepalis facing difficulties abroad, the war in the Middle East, rising fuel prices, and gas cylinder exchange problems.

speakers.name: Samjhana Devkota
speakers.topic: Cyberbullying, social media bill, and government's undemocratic actions

speakers.name: Mohammad Khalid
speakers.topic: Arrest of KP Sharma Oli, issues of Nepalis abroad, and economic concerns

sections.name: Adjournment
sections.summary_en: Honorable Member Mohammad Khalid further addressed the issue of cyberbullying against women and children, emphasizing its impact on social values and family honor. He urged the government to enact strict laws and activate the Cyber Bureau to control cybercrime. He also congratulated the newly elected Vice-President and committee chairpersons. The session concluded with the Chairperson announcing the next speaker.

speakers.topic: Cyberbullying, women's safety, and legislative action

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: Honorable Member Mohammad Khalid congratulated newly elected members and wished them success. He also congratulated the Rastriya Swatantra Party for their electoral success and the new government. He emphasized the importance of unity and cooperation for national progress. Honorable Member Tul Prasad Bishwakarma spoke about the escalating conflict in the Middle East, criticizing US foreign policy and its impact on global peace and stability, including its effects on Nepal. Honorable Member Narayan Datta Bhatta congratulated the elected officials and expressed concerns about the safety of Nepalis abroad, rising inflation, and the government's approach to governance and justice, questioning the accountability of ministers regarding specific incidents.

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: Honorable Member Bhuwan Bahadur Sunar raised concerns about the resurfacing issue of tenant farmers' rights on agricultural land, referencing constitutional provisions and the need for scientific land reform. He also highlighted the importance of irrigation for agricultural productivity and the delayed construction of the Budhi Gandaki reservoir, along with the reopening of industries and airport maintenance.

speakers.name: Bhuwan Bahadur Sunar
speakers.topic: Tenant farmers' rights, land reform, irrigation, infrastructure projects

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: Honorable Member Meena Singh Rakhal addressed the critical issue of violence against women, particularly cyber violence, in the context of technological advancement. She emphasized the inadequacy of current laws and the weak faith in the justice system, calling for stricter laws, effective implementation, and increased public awareness.

speakers.name: Meena Singh Rakhal
speakers.topic: Violence against women, cyber violence, legal reform

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: Honorable Member Khamm Bahadur Khanti congratulated the newly elected committee chairpersons and reflected on the unity displayed in the National Assembly. He discussed the electoral outcome, emphasizing the need for the government to act as a guardian, uphold the constitution, and ensure equal opportunities. He also raised concerns about orchestrated efforts to destabilize major political parties and the importance of a strong opposition.

Another member raises concerns about the international conflict in the Middle East and the government's silence, as well as the issue of inflation and discriminatory policies against journalists. The member also criticizes the amendment to the Money Laundering Act and the filing of false cases.

The member strongly opposes the government's decision to dissolve student unions, calling it undemocratic and demanding its reversal. The member also discusses the nature of elections and the possibility of high-tech fraud.

The member emphasizes that the National Assembly will support good work and oppose bad work, regardless of party affiliation. The member also criticizes the narrative of 'new is good, old is bad' and warns of potential national liberation war if the government acts against national interest.

sections.summary_en: Honorable Member Bishnu Kumari Sapkota congratulated newly elected members and paid tribute to martyrs. She discussed the Janji movement, corruption, and administrative delays, emphasizing the need for impartial investigation. She also praised the government's initiatives for provincial development and cabinet appointments, while cautioning against deviations and highlighting challenges like border issues and youth employment. She also raised concerns about cyberbullying and disaster preparedness.
